title: Proposal for a new client (editable template)
audience: Owners, office staff and account managers who write a written proposal for a new client, whether the job is at a home or a business site
learningOutcomes: Complete every field of the proposal so that a client can read it without asking what an item means
Write a commitment statement and a references section that the business can support with evidence or written consent
Build a price table in Australian dollars that states the GST position and shows how each line was calculated
Use product and environmental claims only where the business holds evidence it can show on request

instruction.heading: What a proposal does
instruction.body: A proposal is the document a prospective client reads after a first contact, a call on the phone or a site visit. It has to answer three questions in a fixed order: who is making the offer and whether the client has reason to trust them, what exactly the business will do in the client's space, and what that work will cost. This template keeps those answers in separate sections so the price never appears without the scope beside it. A proposal is not the agreement. The binding terms sit in the client service agreement (“Client service agreement”) and the quote terms in “Quote and proposal”, and this lesson refers to them without repeating them. The scope method is taught in “Scope of works for a service site”, and the hours-based pricing method is taught in “Pricing by hours per project”. The pricing worksheet (“Pricing and margin worksheet”) produces the numbers that go into the price table.

instruction.heading: Describe the business with facts you can check
instruction.body: Claims about the business are where a proposal most often goes wrong. Years in operation, team size, training and any awards must each match what the business can show. Write the years as a whole number and record the month and year the business started trading, so the figure can be checked against records. The team table lists the people who will attend the site, their role on this job and how long each person has worked for the firm. Do not list someone who is not rostered to the job, because a proposal that names a person who never arrives damages the trust it was written to build. A commitment statement such as a promise of punctuality is only useful if the business records its punctuality and can produce that record. Write each promise as something that can be measured.

instruction.heading: References with written consent
instruction.body: A reference is a person who has agreed that a prospective client may contact them. Ask each person before their name goes into the proposal, and record the date and what they are willing to talk about. A testimonial written for a different service, a different business or a different year should be labelled as such, or left out. Edited, merged or invented testimonials should not be used. Check the misleading-conduct rules in the Australian Consumer Law against current guidance before relying on any testimonial.

instruction.heading: Products, methods and environmental claims
instruction.body: List the products and methods the team uses, and the surface or task each one suits. A product list with no purpose attached adds length without giving the client anything to check. Environmental and health claims are the highest-risk part of this section. Words such as natural, non-toxic, non-hazardous or eco-friendly need evidence the business holds, such as a product label, a safety data sheet or a certification, and the claim must match what that evidence says. Where the evidence is thin, describe what the business does instead, for example which products are used on which surfaces and which are avoided.

instruction.heading: Pricing with GST and a visible basis
instruction.body: Show each price in Australian dollars and state whether the amounts include GST. Each line in the price table needs a unit, such as per visit, per hour, per room or per square metre, and a quantity that matches the scope. The line totals are the rate multiplied by the quantity, and the total is the sum of the lines less any offer. Show a discount as a reduction from the full price the business has charged for the same service on other occasions. Write the offer with its condition and its end date, and check the price display rules in the Australian Consumer Law before using it. The ATO GST registration page gives a turnover threshold of $75,000 or more, or $150,000 or more for a non-profit organisation. Check the GST rate and how GST must appear on a quote with the Australian Taxation Office or a qualified adviser. If prices change before a client accepts, honour a proposal already issued at the old rate, and give repeat customers two to four weeks' notice of a new rate.

instruction.heading: Inclusions, exclusions, complaints and acceptance
instruction.body: State what is included and what is not, taken from the scope of works rather than from a generic list. Where the proposal and the agreement could conflict, the agreement wording should be checked first and the proposal corrected. A satisfaction statement is useful only when it names the complaint route and a response time the business can meet. Check before use whether a line in a proposal can affect a consumer guarantee under the Australian Consumer Law. Check any satisfaction or liability wording against the Australian Consumer Law before use. Keep the acceptance block simple: the method of acceptance, such as a signature or a written reply that quotes the proposal reference, and the date it is recorded.

procedure: Complete the sender and client block, and set the proposal reference and the valid-until date.
Enter the years in operation as a number, with the start month and year, from the business records.
List only the people rostered to this job in the team table, with their role and length of service.
Write the commitment statement as two or three measurable promises, and check each promise against the business's own records.
Ask each reference for written consent, then enter the references table with the consent date.
Describe the service, the areas and tasks, and how often each area is attended, using the scope of works.
List the products and methods, then name the evidence the client can request for each product or environmental claim, deleting any claim with no evidence.
Build the price table from the pricing worksheet, with unit, quantity, rate and line total for each row, and state the GST position.
Describe any offer with its condition and end date, then calculate the total from the table.
Write the inclusions, exclusions and the complaint route, and check them against the service agreement.
Record the acceptance method, then save the completed proposal with its reference, date and version.

workedExamples.situation: A two-person team proposes a fortnightly visit for a three-bedroom home. The owner wants to add a 'free first visit' and a line saying the work is fully guaranteed.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Which wording can stay as written, which must be checked before use, and what should replace the guarantee line?
workedExamples.reasoning: The fortnightly visit and its price can be stated directly from the scope and the pricing worksheet. The 'free first visit' can be shown as a reduction only if the business normally charges for that visit, so the wording needs the condition and an end date, and the price table should show the full price before the offer. The 'fully guaranteed' line has no condition and no route for a complaint. It should be replaced with a statement of how a concern is raised, the response time the business can meet, and a reference to the complaint steps in the agreement.

workedExamples.situation: An office manager wants to list a former client as a reference, but the client has not replied to the request for consent.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Can the name go into the proposal, and what should the references table show instead?
workedExamples.reasoning: The name cannot go into the proposal without the client's consent, so the row is removed or left blank with a note that references are available on request once consent is recorded. The lesson does not treat silence as consent. The proposal stays accurate, and the business keeps a record of the request and the reply, or the lack of one.

equipmentAndPpe: Scope of works for the site, in the format taught in “Scope of works for a service site”
Pricing worksheet or hours estimate (“Pricing and margin worksheet”, “Pricing by hours per project”)
Product labels and safety data sheets for each product named in the proposal
Written consent records for each reference named
PPE: not applicable to this lesson; the proposal is a document

commonErrors.error: Showing a price with no statement of whether GST is included.
commonErrors.prevention: State that the amounts include GST, and show the same basis everywhere a price appears in the proposal.

commonErrors.error: Listing staff who are not rostered to the job.
commonErrors.prevention: Confirm the roster for the first visit before issue, and update the table if the roster changes.

commonErrors.error: Including a product or environmental claim with no evidence on file.
commonErrors.prevention: Name one evidence item per claim the client can request. Delete any claim that has none.

commonErrors.error: Writing an unconditional guarantee with no complaint route.
commonErrors.prevention: Pair every satisfaction statement with the complaint steps, the response time and the remedy used in the agreement.

commonErrors.error: Presenting a 'free' offer that the business never charges for in practice.
commonErrors.prevention: Write the offer with its condition and end date, and show the full price in the table.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: The Australian Consumer Law includes consumer guarantees for services, which the ACCC guidance in R1 summarises. A proposal cannot remove a consumer guarantee by a line of text. Misleading conduct and the display of prices and discounts are also covered by the Australian Consumer Law; check the specific sections and their application to each sentence in this template against a current source, and record the date. Check against the regulator's current guidance or a qualified adviser before issue.

The ATO states that a business must register for GST once its GST turnover reaches $75,000 (other businesses), or $150,000 a year or more for a non-profit organisation, and must register within 21 days once required (ATO page last updated 14 September 2026). Check the GST rate and how GST must be shown on a quote with the ATO. Whether the price shown includes GST must be stated, and the GST display rule has not been confirmed in this template. Registration status must be confirmed with the Australian Taxation Office before any GST statement is relied on.
Check the accuracy and substantiation rules that apply to environmental and health claims about products against a current source, and record the date. Keep the evidence on file for every claim.
Record only the cover the business holds.
This lesson does not grant or confirm any licence, certificate or registration, and completing the proposal does not authorise any regulated work.

qualityStandard: Every field is completed, or marked not applicable with a reason in the field
Each price line shows a unit, quantity, rate and GST position, and the total equals the sum of the lines less any offer
Each reference has a recorded consent date and only names the topics the person agreed to
Each product or environmental claim names an evidence item the client can request, or the claim is removed
Inclusions, exclusions and the complaint route match the service agreement
documentationEvidence: Completed proposal saved with its reference, date and valid-until date
Reference consent records, with name, date and the topics agreed
Product labels or safety data sheet references for each product named
Pricing worksheet reference for each price line
summary: A proposal answers who, what and how much, in that order.
Every claim needs evidence, consent, or removal before issue.
Each price shows its unit, quantity, GST position and basis.
Binding terms live in the agreement, and the proposal refers to them.

editableTemplates.title: Proposal
editableTemplates.purpose: A written proposal that introduces the business and its team, describes the work and its exclusions, shows the price with its basis and GST position, states the complaint route, and asks the client to accept.

fields.label: Sender name and role
fields.prompt: Write the name and role of the person who prepared this proposal.
fields.guidance: The name and role match the person the client will contact. Do not use a shared mailbox name in place of a person.

fields.label: Client name and address
fields.prompt: Write the client's name and the address the service will cover. If the client is a business, add the contact's name and role.
fields.guidance: The address matches the site address that will appear in the service agreement.

fields.label: Reference, date prepared and valid-until date
fields.prompt: Write the proposal reference, the date it was prepared and the date until which the price is valid.
fields.guidance: The reference is unique to the client. The valid-until date is a real date after the preparation date.

fields.label: Years in operation
fields.prompt: Enter the number of full years the business has operated, and the month and year it began trading.
fields.guidance: The number matches the start date that can be shown from business records.

fields.label: Team members on this job
fields.prompt: One row per person who will attend the site. Columns: name, role on this job, years with the business.
fields.guidance: Only people rostered to this job are listed. Years are counted from records, not from memory.

fields.label: Commitment statement
fields.prompt: Write two or three sentences on what the client can expect from the team. Name the work and the standard the business measures against.
fields.guidance: Each promise is one the business can measure or show evidence for. Do not use an unconditional guarantee here. The complaint route is in the field for complaints.

fields.label: Client references
fields.prompt: One row per reference who has agreed to be contacted. Columns: first name and suburb, topics the person agreed to discuss, consent date.
fields.guidance: Every row has a recorded consent date. A reference without consent is removed before the proposal is sent.

fields.label: Service summary
fields.prompt: Describe the service in plain words: what the work is, how often it happens and how long a visit is expected to take.
fields.guidance: Frequency and visit length match the scope of works and the hours estimate.

fields.label: Areas and tasks
fields.prompt: One row per area. Columns: area, task, how often, finish standard.
fields.guidance: Every area in the scope is listed. Each task reads as something the client could check, not a general word such as done.

fields.label: Consultation offer
fields.prompt: Describe any site visit or consultation, whether it is free, what happens at it, and how long it takes.
fields.guidance: States what could change the price after a visit, and how the client is told in writing.

fields.label: Products and methods
fields.prompt: List the products and equipment the team uses, and the surface or task each one suits. Note any product the client has asked the team to avoid.
fields.guidance: Each product is named with its surface or task. Client requests about products are recorded.

fields.label: Evidence for product and environmental claims
fields.prompt: For each product or environmental claim, name the evidence the client can ask to see. Delete any claim that has no evidence.
fields.guidance: Evidence is a label, a safety data sheet or a certificate the business holds. Claims that go beyond the evidence are removed.

fields.label: Price table
fields.prompt: One row per priced item. Columns: item, unit, rate, quantity, line total. State the GST basis in f18.
fields.guidance: Every line has a unit and a quantity that match the scope. Each line total equals the rate multiplied by the quantity.

fields.label: Offer or discount
fields.prompt: Describe any first-time or other offer, its condition and the date it ends. Leave the field as 'none' if there is no offer.
fields.guidance: A discount is shown as a reduction from a price the business genuinely charges. The condition is stated in full.

fields.label: Total (GST basis as stated in f18)
fields.prompt: Enter the total payable for the first visit cycle, after any offer, on the GST basis stated in f18.
fields.guidance: The total equals the price table less any offer. Calculate it from the lines, do not type it from memory.

fields.label: Inclusions and exclusions
fields.prompt: List what is included and what is excluded, using the scope of works.
fields.guidance: Exclusions match the scope and the what-we-will-not-do terms in the service agreement (“Client service agreement”).

fields.label: Complaints and satisfaction wording
fields.prompt: Write the sentences that tell the client how to raise a concern, what the business will do, and by when.
fields.guidance: States the complaint route, the response time and the remedy in plain words. Does not promise a result the business cannot control.

fields.label: Price basis and GST statement
fields.prompt: State the price basis (for example per visit or per hour) and whether the amounts include GST.
fields.guidance: The statement matches the GST position in the pricing worksheet. The GST display rule has not yet been confirmed; check it with the Australian Taxation Office before issue.

fields.label: Acceptance method
fields.prompt: State how the client accepts, for example by signature or by written reply that quotes the proposal reference, and the date the acceptance is recorded.
fields.guidance: The method is one the business can record and file. The acceptance date is kept with the proposal.

levels.meets: Each area names its tasks, frequency and finish standard in words a client could check.
levels.does_not_meet: Areas or tasks are described only in general words, or an area in the scope is missing.

levels.meets: Every product, environmental, experience and reference claim has evidence, a recorded consent, or has been removed.
levels.does_not_meet: A claim remains with no evidence or consent on file.

levels.meets: Each price line shows unit, quantity, rate and GST position, and the total equals the lines less any offer.
levels.does_not_meet: A total cannot be traced to its lines, or a line has no unit or quantity.

levels.meets: Any offer states its condition, the full price it reduces, and its end date.
levels.does_not_meet: An offer has no condition, no end date, or no full price shown.

levels.meets: Inclusions, exclusions and the complaint route match the service agreement and the quote terms.
levels.does_not_meet: The proposal and the agreement state different exclusions, response times or remedies, with no reason given.

outputDocument.title: {{business:business.display_name}} proposal
outputDocument.footer: Prices are shown on the GST basis stated in the pricing section. Prepared by {{business:business.display_name}}, serving {{business:business.service_area}}. Contact {{business:business.support_email}} or {{business:business.support_phone}}.

officialReferences.title: Consumer rights and guarantees (ACCC)
officialReferences.covers: Says services must be carried out with an acceptable level of care and skill, must be fit for any stated purpose, and must be supplied within a reasonable time where no time frame is agreed. Says the basic rights covered by consumer guarantees cannot be taken away by anything a business says or does. Does not confirm the specific sections that apply to each sentence of this template. Publisher: Australian Competition and Consumer Commission. Read through a summary fetch in this pass, not checked against the page text directly.

officialReferences.title: Registering for GST (Australian Taxation Office)
officialReferences.covers: ATO page (last updated 14 September 2026): a business must register once its GST turnover is $75,000 or more, a non-profit organisation once its GST turnover is $150,000 per year or more, and registration must be done within 21 days once it is required. The page does not say how GST must be shown on prices or quotes. Publisher: Australian Taxation Office.

officialReferences.title: Goods and services tax (GST) (Australian Taxation Office)
officialReferences.pageDate: Last updated 21 June 2023 (the only update date shown; 2023-06-21)
officialReferences.covers: Read directly on 2026-11-03. The page does not state a GST rate, does not say GST must be included in prices, and does not say how GST must be shown on quotes or invoices; it points to tax invoice guidance without stating the requirements. The GST rate and display rules therefore remain UNCONFIRMED. Publisher: Australian Taxation Office.
